nodes.label: Bridge/threading: the agent runs in a goroutine; Emit delivers events through a FIFO pipe (eventPipe) — the run's completion (runDoneMsg) rides the same pipe so it can never overtake a streamed delta — because Program.Send blocks on an unbuffered channel and Update runs on the event-loop goroutine (a synchronous emit, e.g. /yolo, would deadlock); the asker blocks the agent on a reply channel; the agent guards its shared state with a mutex so Status() polling is race-free

nodes.label: Refresh: access tokens ~1 h; refresh tokens rotate (~30 d); the lock wait honours the caller's context (polling so Ctrl-C works) and the exchange is bounded at 30 s; invalid_grant keeps the stored entry (moca logout still works) and errors 'session expired … run /login in the TUI, or moca login' (exit 2); a transient failure (network, 429/5xx, timeout) is an *HTTPError/network error the retry layer retries, and a still-live access token is used as is

nodes.label: Streamable HTTP transport: one POST per message (JSON body, Accept both, configured headers with env:VAR resolution); Mcp-Session-Id captured from the initialize response and echoed on every later request; MCP-Protocol-Version sent once negotiated; a JSON response matched by id; an SSE response read until a data: event carries the response with our id; 202 accepted for notifications; a 404 once a session exists → `session expired`; non-2xx → error with a ≤4 KiB body (status checked on notifications too); Close sends DELETE (best-effort, bounded 3 s, under the server lock); without an injected client the manager builds http.Client{Timeout: 15m} (defaultHTTPTimeout) — the TUI's run context is unbounded, so a wedged streaming server must not hang a call forever

nodes.label: Lifecycle Manager: ZERO servers start at session start (index present or not); no server process is spawned except through the manager's ensure (start + initialize + tools/list), which only search (index miss), describe, call and `moca mcp index` reach; search serves from a valid index entry or starts the server once to (re)index; describe/call ensure on demand; the idle timer (mcp.idleTimeout, default 600 s) arms at start and after every call and stops a server only with no call in flight (a busy counter under the server lock, held across the RPC, re-arms at its end — a timer firing between two calls can never kill one); a stopped server stays discoverable via the index and restarts on demand

nodes.label: Dead-transport replay: a call failing with a transport-dead sentinel drops the transport (next use restarts it) and is replayed ONCE only when that cannot run it twice — the request never left (errNotSent: transport already dead or the write failed), the session had expired (the server rejected it unprocessed), or the tool is read-only and non-destructive; any other dead-transport failure is returned as `… (the call may have executed before the connection failed; check before retrying)` — NEVER a text match of server-supplied message (errors.Is on the transports' own sentinels; a tool error containing "exited" must not restart a healthy server)

nodes.label: stdio transport: one JSON object per line on the child's stdin/stdout; a reader goroutine routes responses by id (int64, or a quoted int64 echo), answers server→client ping with {} (anything else -32601), ignores notifications, and logs non-JSON stdout lines plus stderr into a 4 KiB ring; stdout read from a pipe moca OWNS (not cmd.StdoutPipe, whose read end Wait closes under the reader); the exit handler lets the reader drain (bounded 500 ms, also cmd.WaitDelay) so a grandchild holding the pipes cannot stall it and a reply written just before exit is never lost; a process exit fails every pending call with `server <name> exited (<status>): <ring tail>` carrying the errTransportDead sentinel (errors.Is-visible) — also when the write itself fails, surfacing the recorded exit error rather than bare EPIPE; Close kills the process group via tools.SetProcessGroup/KillProcessGroup (5 s bound; a child stuck in uninterruptible sleep must not hang shutdown)

nodes.label: Plan mode in the loop (rev 20/21): while Env.Plan is on, EVERY request appends the plan envelope to EVERY user text message — a request-only transform (the transcript keeps exactly what the user wrote; rev 21: a moving envelope rewrote the previous prompt on each new one and forfeited the prompt cache from there, so the prefix stays byte-stable across prompts) — and a run reaching its natural end without Env.PlanWrote gets ONE bounded nudge (a persisted user message, answered with the envelope again) before it may finish; a second end without the file emits `warning: plan mode: the run finished without a plan file under docs/plans/ — the deliverable is missing` (the maxSteps wrap-up path warns too); when maxSteps ≥ 4 and the plan still does not exist two steps before the wrap-up, a persisted 'running out of steps — write the plan file now' message lands the deliverable instead of only warning
